Feedback

Status

1. Reimagine the Hero Section

  • Rework the hero using our existing brand colours and visual style.
  • Make the Before vs. After Revenue per Visitor comparison the focal point of the hero.
  • Clearly show the starting RPV and the improved RPV so the revenue outcome is immediately obvious.
  • Make the five metrics and their before-and-after states easy to understand at a glance.
  • Visually reinforce that the goal is to optimise all five metrics until they turn green.
  • Ensure the entire hero fits comfortably on screen, with balanced spacing, sizing, and alignment.

2. Make the Revenue Outcome More Prominent

  • Make the RPV numbers larger and more visually striking.
  • Clearly communicate the transformation from the current Revenue per Visitor to the improved Revenue per Visitor.
  • Use colour contrast, typography, and visual hierarchy to make the difference between the two numbers immediately noticeable.
  • Make it obvious that fixing the red metric is what improves the overall RPV.

3. Clarify the Red Metric Explanation

  • Make the statement “Your Red Metric Is What's Keeping Your Revenue Per Visitor at 0.5 to 4.92” easier to understand and more prominent.
  • Clearly connect the underperforming red metric to the current RPV and the potential improvement.
  • Use a simple visual hierarchy so users can immediately identify:
    • Which metric is underperforming.
    • How it is affecting their Revenue per Visitor.
    • What the improved outcome could look like.

4. Improve the Five-Metric Colour System

  • Make the red and green states visually distinct and consistent.
  • Ensure the “Your New Goal: All of These Are Green” section clearly shows all five metrics in green.
  • Keep the before-and-after sections visually balanced, with consistent sizing, spacing, and alignment.
  • Make sure the green states communicate the desired outcome without creating confusion between the current performance and the goal.

5. Make the “About Your Ad Budget” Section Clearer

  • Rework this section so the data is much easier to scan and understand.
  • Make the key numbers, comparisons, and takeaways stand out visually.
  • Improve the hierarchy between the data, supporting explanations, and the main takeaway.
  • Avoid making users work to understand what the numbers mean or why they matter.

6. Ensure All 10 Questions Section is Bold headline

  • Keep all 10 questions section sufficiently large and legible.
  • Ensure the question text is easy to read without feeling cramped or requiring unnecessary effort.
  • Maintain consistent typography, spacing, and layout throughout the questions.

7. Add the “Watch the Workshop” Button (Middle indent it)

  • Position the “Watch the Workshop” button between the relevant sections so users can easily find it.
  • Make the button prominent enough to stand out without disrupting the overall page design.
  • Ensure the placement feels intentional within the user's journey through the page.

8. Create a Separate Workshop Page

  • The workshop should not be embedded in or displayed directly on the results page.
  • Create a dedicated “Watch the Workshop” page.
  • Link the button to this separate page.
  • Please clarify why the dedicated workshop page has not been added yet and ensure it is included in the implementation.
